territory: Directory, places/gazetteer, map, people search: src/app/(main)/directory/** (page.tsx, actions.ts, where.ts WIP), src/lib/{directory-facets,geocode,city-coords,city-scope,map-cluster}.ts, src/app/api/places/search (WIP), src/app/api/users/search (WIP), src/app/api/users-by-batch (WIP), src/components/directory/** (directory-client, alumni-map, profile-card), src/components/common/location-picker.tsx, plus the UserPlace write paths that feed the directory (settings updateUserPlaces WIP, onboarding saveOnboardingRegister) and the Place/UserPlace schema + manual migrations.

findings.title: Non-numeric or non-integer year/yearFrom/yearTo query params reach Prisma Int filters and crash the whole /directory page with a 500
findings.expected: A malformed filter value in the URL (a mangled shared link, a typo, a crawler) degrades to zero results or is ignored; the directory always renders.
findings.actual: `/directory?year=abc` sets `where.batchYear = NaN`; `/directory?year=2009.5` sets a float; `/directory?yearFrom=99999999999` exceeds Int32. All three throw PrismaClientValidationError inside the page's Promise.all (the `prisma.user.count({ where })` at page.tsx:293 runs even with no other filter), so the entire page throws to src/app/error.tsx. The same unvalidated filters flow into the loadDirectoryPage server action.
findings.evidence: where.ts:27-28: `const showingYear = filters.year === "faculty" ? "faculty" : filters.year ? Number(filters.year) : null;` -- Number("abc") is NaN, and `typeof NaN === "number"`, so where.ts:46-47 `} else if (typeof showingYear === "number") { where.batchYear = showingYear; }` assigns NaN to an Int filter. where.ts:29-30 guards NaN for yearFrom/yearTo only via truthiness (`filters.yearFrom ? Number(...) : null` then `if (yearFrom || yearTo)`), which lets non-NaN garbage through: `Number("2009.5")` = 2009.5 is truthy and lands in `{ gte: 2009.5 }` (where.ts:49-53) on the Int column batchYear. Prisma's client validation rejects NaN and non-integer/out-of-range values for Int fields at runtime with a thrown PrismaClientValidationError, and page.tsx has no try/catch around the Promise.all (lines 257-310).
findings.fixDirection: Parse the three numeric params once with a strict guard (e.g. `const n = Number(v); Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 1900 && n <= 2100 ? n : null`) inside buildDirectoryWhere (it is the shared choke point for both the SSR page and the server action), treating anything else as no-filter. Same guard for showingYear in page.tsx:198.
findings.gateOrTest: A unit test on buildDirectoryWhere asserting `year: "abc"`, `year: "2009.5"`, `yearFrom: "1e99"` produce a where without batchYear (add to the existing unit-test suite npm run check executes); live: GET /directory?year=abc must render the empty grid, not the error page.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: navigate to http://localhost:3000/directory?year=abc signed in; observe the error boundary instead of the directory.

findings.title: Directory page serializes every located member (name, batch, job, all cities) into the map props on every load: ~1-2MB of payload and a full-membership query per view at the 2,000-member ceiling
findings.expected: The map payload stays roughly O(number of cities): pins carry coordinates and counts; the people behind a pin are fetched on drilldown.
findings.actual: Every directory render runs `prisma.user.findMany({ where: pinWhere, select: PIN_SELECT })` with no `take` (page.tsx:294-297) over every member with at least one place, and buildPins pushes a full PinPerson (id, name, avatarColor, photoUrl, birdOverride, accountType, verifyState, batchType, batchYear, jobTitle, otherCities) into `people` for EVERY city the person lists (page.tsx:149-165). The whole structure is passed as props (`cityPins`, `unmappedPeople`) and serialized into the RSC payload for every viewer on every visit. At 2,000 members averaging 1.5 cities that is ~3,000 person objects at ~250-400 bytes each, ~0.75-1.2MB before RSC encoding overhead, on a page that is fully dynamic (auth() at page.tsx:196 defeats caching). The 4.5MB Vercel response cap is not hit at 2,000, but mobile members pay seconds of transfer for a map whose visible pins only need counts.
findings.evidence: PIN_SELECT (page.tsx:42-57) selects ten person fields plus `places: { select: { city, lat, lng } }`; the query at page.tsx:294-297 has orderBy but no take: `prisma.user.findMany({ where: pinWhere, select: PIN_SELECT, orderBy: [{ batchYear: "desc" }, { name: "asc" }] })`. buildPins (page.tsx:149-164) does `existing.people.push(person)` per resolvable city. Only the namesLocked branch strips people (page.tsx:333-336); every verified viewer gets the full roll. directory-client.tsx:570-575 hands `cityPins` straight to <AlumniMap>.
findings.fixDirection: Ship pins as {city, lng, lat, count} plus a small top-N preview, and fetch a city's people on drilldown via a paginated server action (the drilldown Sheet in alumni-map.tsx is already a natural fetch boundary); alternatively cap PinPerson to {id, name, photoUrl, birdOverride, batchType, batchYear} and drop places/jobTitle/otherCities from the payload to roughly halve it. Keep the aggregation query but select only what buildPins needs for counting.
findings.gateOrTest: A size assertion in an e2e/unit check: rendered /directory HTML+RSC payload under a budget (e.g. 300KB) with a seeded 2,000-member dataset; or a unit test that CityPin.people is never serialized beyond the preview cap.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: curl the authed /directory response on dev and measure body size; scale reasoning is arithmetic from the quoted query.

findings.title: places/search runs a sequential scan of all 234,934 Place rows on every keystroke of 4 or more characters (the altNames ILIKE arm defeats both expression indexes), with no cap on query length
findings.expected: The type-ahead stays on the indexed prefix path; per-keystroke cost is an index range scan plus a small sort.
findings.actual: For queries of 4+ characters (i.e. most of the keystrokes of any real city name), the WHERE becomes `lower(asciiName) LIKE 'q%' OR lower(name) LIKE 'q%' OR altNames ILIKE '%q%'`. Because the third arm has no index (altNames has none, and '%q%' is unindexable by btree anyway), Postgres cannot BitmapOr the clause and must sequential-scan the whole 234k-row table, running three pattern matches per row (altNames is a long comma list). Typing "bengaluru" fires ~6 such scans. The route's own comment (lines 20-23) claims the 4-char gate stops short queries from forcing a seq scan, but every long query forces one. On the shared Supabase instance (one DB for prod AND local dev) a launch-day burst of members filling in their cities stacks 50-150ms scans; q is also unbounded in length (route.ts:89 only checks `raw.length < 1`), so a pathological 10KB query multiplies per-row match cost. Rate limit is 120/min/user (rate-limit.ts:94) and fail-open.
findings.evidence: route.ts:99-102: `const altNamesClause = raw.length >= 4 ? Prisma.sql`OR "altNames" ILIKE ${containsPattern} ESCAPE '\\'` : Prisma.empty;` spliced into the WHERE at route.ts:104-109. The only indexes on Place are the two lower() text_pattern_ops expression indexes (round6.sql:30-31), which serve the two prefix arms but nothing serves altNames. An OR with one unindexable arm forces a full table scan in Postgres. Secondary: even prefix-only queries of 1 char sort every match ('a%' is tens of thousands of rows) before LIMIT 8 (route.ts:110-119), a top-N sort per keystroke.
findings.fixDirection: Add a pg_trgm GIN index on altNames (manual migration, consistent with the existing hand-applied index policy) so the ILIKE arm is indexable, or restructure as UNION ALL of the two indexed prefix arms LIMIT 8 plus a separately LIMITed altNames arm only when the prefix arms return nothing. Independently cap raw query length (e.g. slice to 80 chars) and consider raising the minimum length for the altNames arm.
findings.gateOrTest: EXPLAIN (via a read-only run-sql inspection by the fix session) showing no Seq Scan on Place for a 6-char query; a regression note in the route comment. Optionally a timing assertion in a script hitting /api/places/search.
findings.reproPlan: Read-only: EXPLAIN SELECT with the exact quoted WHERE against the live Place table (read-only query), compare plans with and without the altNames arm.

findings.title: updateUserPlaces (settings) accepts a completely unvalidated payload: unbounded label/city strings poison the shared city facet and map for every member, and non-string/non-finite fields crash the action
findings.expected: Every server action Zod-validates everything including shapes and lengths (the codebase's own write-path invariant); the sibling onboarding action does exactly this with placeSchema (label/city max 160, z.number() lat/lng).
findings.actual: updateUserPlaces (settings/actions.ts:144-186) takes `places: { placeId: number|null; label: string; city: string; lat: number|null; lng: number|null }[]` and never validates it: (a) label/city have no length cap, so one crafted call (any authed account, no verified-email gate, no rate limit on this action) can store city strings up to the ~1MB server-action body limit; those strings then flow into `prisma.userPlace.groupBy({ by: ["city"] })` (page.tsx:304-309) and are serialized into EVERY member's directory page as facet options, and into the map pipeline; (b) a non-string label throws TypeError at `p.label.trim()` (line 158 via 153); (c) lat/lng are written through unchecked, so out-of-range or junk floats place the member anywhere on the map (page.tsx placeCoords trusts row lat/lng first, line 83).
findings.evidence: settings/actions.ts:150-159: `const cleaned = places.map((p) => ({ placeId: p.placeId, label: titleCase(p.label.trim()), city: titleCase(p.city.trim()), lat: p.lat, lng: p.lng })).filter((p) => p.label.length > 0).slice(0, 30);` -- the only bound is the 30-item slice. Contrast onboarding/actions.ts:22-28: `const placeSchema = z.object({ placeId: z.number().int().nullable(), label: z.string().trim().min(1).max(160), city: z.string().trim().min(1).max(160), lat: z.number().nullable(), lng: z.number().nullable() });` -- the same data shape, properly fenced, proving the intended contract.
findings.fixDirection: Reuse (export) the onboarding placeSchema and run `z.array(placeSchema).max(30).safeParse(places)` at the top of updateUserPlaces; add lat -90..90 / lng -180..180 range checks to the shared schema; consider the same schema in the admin people action's place write (admin/people/actions.ts:151-160) for consistency.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test calling updateUserPlaces with a 10k-char label, a numeric label, and lat=9999 asserting a clean validation error, added to the checked-in test suite.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (a live proof would write junk rows into the ONE shared production database).

findings.title: Load more race: a late page-2 response fetched under the OLD filters is appended into the NEW filter's results and clobbers the new cursor
findings.expected: Changing a filter invalidates any in-flight pagination request; results shown always belong to the active filter set.
findings.actual: Click "Load more" under filter A, then switch to filter B before the action resolves: the useEffect at lines 126-131 resets results/cursor to B's first page when the new server props land, and when the stale A request then resolves, `setResults((prev) => [...prev, ...data.users...])` (line 150-153) appends A's page-2 people into B's list and `setCursor(data.nextCursor)` (line 154) installs A's cursor, so the next Load more continues paging A's result set under B's UI.
findings.evidence: handleLoadMore (lines 133-156) captures no request generation and checks nothing on resolution: `const data = await loadDirectoryPage({ filters: {...initialFilters...}, cursor }); setResults((prev) => { const seen = new Set(prev.map((u) => u.id)); return [...prev, ...data.users.filter((u) => !seen.has(u.id))]; }); setCursor(data.nextCursor);` while the effect at 126-131 (`setResults(users); setCursor(nextCursor);` on `[users, nextCursor, hasFilter]`) can run between the await's start and finish. No AbortController, no monotonic request id (contrast usePlaceSearch in location-picker.tsx:131-167, which does exactly this guard).
findings.fixDirection: Add a generation counter ref incremented both in the props-reset effect and at the start of handleLoadMore; discard the response if the generation moved (same pattern as usePlaceSearch's requestIdRef).
findings.gateOrTest: A Playwright spec (written after MCP confirmation, per house rules) throttling the action and asserting the grid contains only the second filter's people; minimally a unit-level note pinned in the component.
findings.reproPlan: Live: chrome-devtools MCP with network throttling; filter to a city, click Load more, immediately switch filters, observe foreign rows appended.

findings.title: Load more has no error handling: one failed server-action call leaves the button stuck on "Loading..." forever with no retry or message
findings.expected: Chaos rule 6k: DB slow/down mid-request shows the member something actionable (an error toast and a re-enabled button).
findings.actual: If loadDirectoryPage rejects (network blip, DB down, or the Prisma validation crash from the year-params finding), the awaited promise throws out of handleLoadMore: `setLoadingMore(false)` on line 155 never runs, the rejection is unhandled (event-handler errors do not hit React error boundaries), and the button at lines 530-540 renders disabled with "Loading..." until a full page reload. The rest of the list is unreachable.
findings.evidence: handleLoadMore (lines 133-156) has no try/catch/finally: `setLoadingMore(true); const data = await loadDirectoryPage({...}); ... setLoadingMore(false);`. Button: `<Button variant="outline" onClick={handleLoadMore} disabled={loadingMore} ...>{loadingMore ? "Loading..." : "Load more"}</Button>`.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap the await in try/finally (finally: setLoadingMore(false)); on catch, toast the shared failure copy (Sonner is already the app pattern) and leave cursor intact so the click can be retried.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit/Playwright: mock the action to reject once and assert the button returns to "Load more" and a toast appears.
findings.reproPlan: Live: chrome-devtools MCP, set network offline after first page, click Load more, observe the permanently disabled button.

findings.title: "Batch: newest first" sort lists every member with NO batch year first (Postgres DESC = NULLS FIRST), and keyset Load more over the null sort key risks silent truncation
findings.expected: Batch-desc shows the newest batches first; members without a batch year (teachers who set type filters off, mid-school leavers) sort last; pagination walks the full result set.
findings.actual: directoryOrderBy returns `[{ batchYear: "desc" }, ...]` with no nulls option, which Prisma compiles to `ORDER BY "batchYear" DESC` -- NULLS FIRST in Postgres -- so page 1 of "Batch: newest first" opens with the null-batch members. Secondary (suspected): when the 60th row of a page has batchYear NULL, the cursor row's null sort key makes Prisma's cursor row-comparison involve NULL, a known Prisma cursor-pagination hazard that can return an empty next page and silently end the list.
findings.evidence: where.ts:92-94: `case "batch-desc": return [{ batchYear: "desc" as const }, { name: "asc" as const }, { id: "asc" as const }];` -- Prisma supports `{ sort: "desc", nulls: "last" }` and it is not used. The pagination in actions.ts:65-71 cursors on `{ id: cursor }` while ordering by the nullable batchYear. batchYear is nullable by design (schema.prisma:37 `batchYear Int?`, null for teachers and mid-school leavers) and teacher rows exist (facultyCount tile renders).
findings.fixDirection: Use `{ batchYear: { sort: "desc", nulls: "last" } }` (and `nulls: "last"` on batch-asc for symmetry); for the cursor half, verify Prisma 7's generated SQL for a null cursor sort key and, if broken, exclude `batchYear: null` rows from batch-sorted queries or append them as a final unsorted segment.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on directoryOrderBy asserting the nulls option; live check that /directory?type=teachers&sort=batch-desc no longer leads with null-batch rows; a seeded pagination test crossing a null-batch page boundary.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: open /directory?sort=batch-desc with any filter matching a null-batch member and read the first rows; for the cursor half, inspect the generated SQL via prisma log in dev (read-only).

findings.title: Hard-deleted cursor row (retention purge or admin delete between pages) makes Load more return empty and silently ends the directory list early
findings.expected: Pagination survives a row disappearing between pages: the next page continues from the surviving neighbours.
findings.actual: The cursor is the raw id of the last displayed row (`cursor: { id: cursor }, skip: 1`). Prisma cursor pagination resolves the cursor row by unique id to anchor the sort position; when that row no longer exists (the 60-day deletion sweep purges User rows outright; admin deletes too), Prisma's documented behaviour is to return no rows, so the member's Load more yields `{ users: [], nextCursor: null }` and the tail of the result set is unreachable until they reload with fresh filters. Note: a row that is merely blocked/deletion-requested still exists, so only hard deletion triggers this.
findings.evidence: actions.ts:65-71: `const rows = await prisma.user.findMany({ where, select: PERSON_SELECT, orderBy, take: PAGE_SIZE + 1, ...(cursor ? { cursor: { id: cursor }, skip: 1 } : {}) });` -- no existence fallback, and nextCursor becomes null on an empty page (lines 73-76), which the client treats as end-of-list (directory-client.tsx:530 `{cursor && ...}` hides the button). The purge mechanism is real: User.deletionRequestedAt doc (schema.prisma:62-68) says the retention sweep "purges the row".
findings.fixDirection: Move to a where-based keyset (compare on the composite sort tuple, e.g. `(createdAt, batchYear, id) < (...)` values carried in the cursor token) instead of Prisma's row-anchored cursor, or on an empty page with a cursor retry once without the cursor from the last known sort values. Marked suspected only because Prisma 7's exact empty-result behaviour for a missing cursor row should be confirmed once in dev before the rework.
findings.gateOrTest: A seeded test: fetch page 1, delete the boundary row, fetch page 2, assert the remaining rows still arrive.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only against production data; provable in dev only with a disposable row, which is a write -- leave to the fix session.

findings.title: LocationPicker silently converts every city to a free-typed, coordinate-less entry when /api/places/search fails or is rate-limited, dropping members off the map
findings.expected: A transient search failure is presented as a failure (retry affordance), not as "this place does not exist"; gazetteer-known cities keep their coordinates.
findings.actual: On any non-OK response (429 from the shared 120/min search limiter, 500, network error) the fetch is rejected, the catch sets `results = []`, and the options memo then offers only the freeText fallback row ("Use it as typed ... Not in our list -- we'll save it as typed"). A member typing "Bengaluru" during an outage saves `{ placeId: null, lat: null, lng: null }`; the row only stays on the map because the legacy metros table happens to cover it -- any city outside city-coords.ts and the gazetteer's exact-name fallback lands in the Unmapped bucket permanently, with no signal to the member that anything went wrong.
findings.evidence: location-picker.tsx:155: `.then((res) => (res.ok ? res.json() : Promise.reject(new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`))))` then 160-164: `.catch((err) => { ... setResults([]); })`; options memo 198-205: `if (trimmed && !loading && results.length === 0) { placeOptions.push({ kind: "freeText", text: trimmed }); }` -- the error state and the genuinely-not-found state are indistinguishable. toSelection (line 95) stores `{ placeId: null, ..., lat: null, lng: null }`. The shared "search" limit (rate-limit.ts:94, 120/min) is spent by all three lookup endpoints, so heavy people-picker use in the same minute can 429 this one.
findings.fixDirection: Track an error flag in usePlaceSearch distinct from empty results; on error, render a "Search is unavailable, try again" row instead of the freeText option (keep freeText for genuine zero-hit responses). Optionally retry once on 429 after the reset window hint.
findings.gateOrTest: Component test: mock fetch to 429 and assert the freeText option is NOT offered; the error row is.
findings.reproPlan: Live: chrome-devtools MCP, block /api/places/search via network conditions, type a known city in the settings picker, observe the "Use it as typed" row.

findings.title: City and House filters match by substring: filtering one city/house also returns members of any city/house that contains it as a substring
findings.expected: Picking "Salem" from the city facet returns Salem members; picking a house returns members of that house.
findings.actual: The city filter compiles to `places.some.city CONTAINS variant` (insensitive), so "Salem" matches "Winston-Salem", "York" matches "New York" -- and the facet options come from distinct real UserPlace.city values, so both the contained and containing names appear as separate options that cross-match. The house filter is `houses CONTAINS house` over the JSON string `[{"year":2003,"house":"Golden"}]`, so a free-typed "Other" house like "Silver Oak" is returned by the canonical "Silver" filter, and a crafted `?house=200` URL matches the year digits of nearly everyone with any house entry.
findings.evidence: where.ts:61-63: `where.places = { some: { OR: targets.map((v) => ({ city: { contains: escapeLike(v), ...insensitive } })) } };` and where.ts:70: `if (filters.house) where.houses = { contains: escapeLike(filters.house) };` -- houses is `String?` holding JSON (schema.prisma:23). The Delhi/New Delhi case is deliberately unified by cityNameVariants (same coords in CITY_COORDS), but that mechanism does not exist for unrelated substring pairs.
findings.fixDirection: City: use `equals` with insensitive mode against each variant (the facet values are exact stored city strings, so equality loses nothing). House: match the JSON shape, e.g. contains on the quoted token `"house":"Golden"` (values are normalized by normalizeHouse so the serialized form is stable), or filter in SQL with a JSON operator.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit tests on buildDirectoryWhere: city "Salem" must not match a places row "Winston-Salem"; house "Silver" must not match houses JSON containing "Silver Oak"; house "200" must match nothing.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: /directory?city=York (if both cities exist in data) or code-argument-only.

findings.title: users-by-batch: non-integer numeric values in ?batches= reach a Prisma Int `in` filter and 500 the route
findings.expected: Garbage batch values are dropped (as NaN and 0 already are) and the route answers with an empty list.
findings.actual: `?batches=2009.5` or `?batches=Infinity` survives `.map(Number).filter(Boolean)` (2009.5 and Infinity are truthy) and lands in `batchYear: { in: batches }`; Prisma's Int validation throws, the route has no try/catch, and the caller gets a 500 instead of `{ userIds: [] }`.
findings.evidence: route.ts:32: `const batches = (searchParams.get("batches")?.split(",").map(Number).filter(Boolean) || []).slice(0, 120);` -- filter(Boolean) removes NaN and 0 but keeps floats and Infinity. route.ts:44-46: `where: { batchYear: { in: batches }, ... }` with no error handling in the handler.
findings.fixDirection: Replace filter(Boolean) with `.filter((n) => Number.isInteger(n) && n > 1900 && n < 2100)` (mirrors the intent of the ~108-possible-years comment above it).
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test or route test: GET /api/users-by-batch?batches=2009.5 returns 200 with empty userIds.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: authed GET /api/users-by-batch?batches=2009.5 on dev; expect 500 today.

findings.title: Directory search debounce timer survives unmount: navigating away within 300ms of typing yanks the member back to /directory
findings.expected: Leaving the directory cancels any pending search navigation.
findings.actual: handleSearch schedules `setTimeout(() => updateFilters("q", value), 300)` (line 185) and nothing clears it on unmount; router.push inside updateFilters still fires after the member has clicked through to a profile card, navigating them back to /directory?q=... mid-read.
findings.evidence: Lines 181-188: `const handleSearch = useCallback((value: string) => { setQuery(value); if (searchTimer.current) clearTimeout(searchTimer.current); searchTimer.current = setTimeout(() => updateFilters("q", value), 300); }, [updateFilters]);` -- there is no `useEffect(() => () => clearTimeout(searchTimer.current), [])` anywhere in the component.
findings.fixDirection: Add an unmount cleanup effect clearing searchTimer.current.
findings.gateOrTest: Playwright: type a character and click a profile card within 300ms; assert the URL stays on /profile/[id].
findings.reproPlan: Live: chrome-devtools MCP, type in the search box and immediately click a result; watch the URL bounce back.

findings.title: Search telemetry (logSearch) is fire-and-forget with no after()/waitUntil: on Vercel the write can be frozen with the function and lost
findings.expected: Work that must outlive the response is scheduled via next/server after() (or waitUntil), per taxonomy 6f; the owner's "most common searches" question depends on these rows actually landing.
findings.actual: Both routes call `void logSearch({...})` immediately before returning the response. logSearch performs up to two sequential Prisma round trips (dedupe findFirst, then create/update); once the response is returned Vercel may freeze the lambda before those complete, so an unknown fraction of searches (biased toward fast responses, i.e. most of them) is silently never recorded. The in-code "fire-and-forget" comment covers swallowing errors, not serverless suspension.
findings.evidence: places route.ts:127-133: `void logSearch({ scope: "places", query: raw, userId: session?.user?.id, results: results.length }); return NextResponse.json(results);` (identical shape at users/search route.ts:72-79). grep confirms neither file references after( anywhere. search-log.ts:50-79 shows the two-query write that must survive the response.
findings.fixDirection: Wrap the call in `after(() => logSearch({...}))` from next/server in both routes (and audit the feed's logSearch call site for the same shape while there).
findings.gateOrTest: A grep-style regression check (the repo already pins patterns in security-regressions.test.mjs) asserting logSearch call sites are inside after(); observable fix: SearchLog rows appear reliably in production.
findings.reproPlan: code-argument-only (loss is probabilistic on the platform; locally the process never freezes).

findings.title: A batch-tile year filter is silently overridden by the batch-range facet while both render as active filter tokens
findings.expected: Filters shown as active in the sentence line all constrain the results, or conflicting ones are merged/cleared.
findings.actual: Drill into a batch tile (?year=2009), then set a batch range in the Filters panel: where.ts assigns `where.batchYear = 2009` (line 47) and then unconditionally overwrites it with the range object (lines 49-54), so the tile filter does nothing -- yet the sentence line still shows BOTH tokens ("Batch of '09" at client 251-257 and the range at 229-235), and the result count reflects only the range.
findings.evidence: where.ts:44-54: `} else if (typeof showingYear === "number") { where.batchYear = showingYear; } if (yearFrom || yearTo) { where.batchYear = { ...(yearFrom ? { gte: yearFrom } : {}), ...(yearTo ? { lte: yearTo } : {}) }; }` -- plain property overwrite, no reconciliation and no removal of the year token client-side.
findings.fixDirection: In updateBatchRange (client), delete the `year` param when setting a range (and vice versa in the tile handler), so the URL can never carry both; or intersect them server-side.
findings.gateOrTest: Unit test on buildDirectoryWhere({year:"2009", yearFrom:"2015"}) asserting a deliberate resolution; UI test that setting a range clears the year token.
findings.reproPlan: Live read-only: open /directory?year=2009&yearFrom=2015&yearTo=2020 and compare tokens vs results.

verifiedClean: 6c double-submit on Load more: rapid double-click issues duplicate requests but results are deduped by id (directory-client.tsx:150-153 seen-Set) and identical cursors converge -- no duplicate rows, no corruption

6d UserPlace position races: both write paths replace the list wholesale inside one $transaction (settings/actions.ts:162-181 array form; onboarding/actions.ts:78-106 short interactive tx) -- concurrent saves are last-writer-wins with no interleaved/duplicate-position state; array-form transactions are pgbouncer-safe and the interactive one is 3 statements, well under the 5s window

6d/6j Place prefix-search index assumption: the live indexes ARE lower() text_pattern_ops expression indexes (migrations-manual/2026-07-18-round6.sql:30-31), which serve both LIKE 'prefix%' arms of places/search AND geocode.ts's lower() IN equality (pattern-ops btrees support plain equality) -- the core index assumption holds; only the altNames arm breaks it (reported)

$queryRaw parameterization: both raw queries (places/search route.ts:104-120, geocode.ts:84-90) use Prisma.sql tagged templates with bound parameters, escapeLike on user input, and ESCAPE '\' -- no injection or wildcard leakage

Blocked / deletion-requested / deleted member exclusion is consistent across EVERY directory read path: grid where (where.ts:34), both pinWhere branches (page.tsx:249-251), batch tiles, faculty count, batch range (page.tsx:266-279), city facet groupBy (page.tsx:304-309), users/search (route.ts:42-45), users-by-batch (route.ts:44-50)

Stage-1 namesLocked stripping happens server-side BEFORE serialization everywhere: page.tsx:333-336 empties pin people, page.tsx:280 skips the grid query, actions.ts:59-60 gates the action, users/search and users-by-batch both call requireVerifiedEmail -- view-source has nothing to find
users-by-batch response size: hard take:5000 (route.ts:59), ~150KB id-only / ~600KB detail worst case, comfortably under the 4.5MB Vercel cap; IN list capped at 120 entries

Null-island / null-coordinate handling: placeCoords uses `!= null` (page.tsx:83), not falsiness, so a legitimate 0 coordinate survives; unprojectable points become NaN and buildGroups drops them (map-cluster.ts:136-138, alumni-map.tsx:182-184) instead of plotting at 0,0; group member indices stay aligned with the pins array (geom is index-preserving map, filter happens at group creation)

Map clustering maths: O(n^2) passes bounded (MAX_MERGE_PASSES 16), deterministic sort and keys (min-member partition keys cannot collide), ring fallback at the zoom ceiling, div-by-zero at dist=0 clamped by ZOOM_CEILING, maxZoom floor 12 for sparse data -- examined against 0/1/duplicate-coordinate/antimeridian inputs, no crash path found
usePlaceSearch out-of-order guard: requestIdRef + AbortController correctly discard stale type-ahead responses (location-picker.tsx:131-171)
cityNameVariants prototype-pollution guard: Object.hasOwn protects against ?city=constructor (city-coords.ts:144)

IST/UTC date math: the directory renders no member-facing dates; the only Date use is a getFullYear fallback for slider bounds when zero users have batch years (page.tsx:355-356) -- no day-boundary logic to shift

Empty states: zero-result grid (hoopoe card), empty map (two-message card), namesLocked cards, empty drilldown, brand-new member with no places (excluded from map by places.some guard, still searchable by name) -- all present in directory-client.tsx:483-563 and alumni-map.tsx:652-660
escapeLike application: q, every city variant, and house are escaped (where.ts:36, 62, 70); profession is equality; consistent with the db-text contract
Rate limiting present on all three lookup endpoints via the shared 'search' limiter (fail-open posture is a tracked, deliberate design)
